T1003.reason: SysinternalsSuite staged in Downloads, accessChk/PsExec/sdelete run from user paths, python.exe dropped in C:\Windows\Temp on nashua and later wiped.

T1003.001.name: LSASS Memory
T1003.001.reason: PowerShell-compiled DLLs (csc.exe) followed by lsass.exe handles 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff with UNKNOWN call-trace frames on scranton; wsmprovhost 0x1f3fff on nashua.

T1003.002.name: Security Account Manager
T1003.002.reason: No SAM/SECURITY hive access, reg save, or hive copy events.

T1003.003.name: NTDS
T1003.003.reason: No ntds/ntdsutil/vssadmin activity in sysmon or 4688 command lines.

T1003.004.name: LSA Secrets
T1003.004.reason: pbeesly's processes (including C:\ProgramData\victim\â€®cod.3aka3.scr) read \REGISTRY\MACHINE\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Lsa; the 4662 Policy\Secrets\$MACHINE.ACC events were benign LOCAL SERVICE machine-account access.

T1003.006.name: DCSync
T1003.006.reason: Single 4662 with DS-Replication-Get-Changes was performed by the NEWYORK$ machine account on its own DC; no drsuapi/lsadump/DCSync tooling anywhere.

T1040.name: Network Sniffing
T1040.reason: The only capture-tooling command lines were two netsh.exe 'trace start capture=yes'/'trace stop' invocations on scranton.dmevals.local whose parent is the Azure Network Watcher agent (NetworkWatcherAgent.exe), followed by Azure guest-agent logman.exe ETL traces into C:\WindowsAzure\Logs. No pcap/npcap/wpcap image loads (C049 zero), no pktmon/dumpcap/windump/rawcap/Wireshark/tcpdump process creation, no PowerShell capture script blocks (C050 zero). The non-standard javamtsup service is a SysinternalsSuite artifact extracted by pbeesly, not a capture driver. Zeek window shows only normal AD/web traffic plus self-signed-cert notices.

T1056.name: Input Capture
T1056.reason: Input capture confirmed on scranton.dmevals.local: PowerShell Invoke-ScreenCapture loop plus Get-Clipboard by user pbeesly, followed by Remove-Job cleanup.

T1056.001.name: Keylogging
T1056.001.reason: No keylogger indicators in process creation, PowerShell script blocks, service installs or registry writes; capture was GUI/clipboard based.

T1056.002.name: GUI Input Capture
T1056.002.reason: hostui.exe launched by PowerShell and read Explorer.EXE memory (0x1400) one second later; no direct clipboard artifact captured.

T1056.003.name: Web Portal Capture
T1056.003.reason: No IIS/web-shell artifacts, no inetpub/aspx file or object access, and no credential-portal HTTP POSTs in Zeek.

T1056.004.name: Credential API Hooking
T1056.004.reason: powershell.exe (0x1000) and wsmprovhost.exe (0x1f3fff) opened handles to lsass.exe on scranton and nashua; no injected hooking DLLs observed.

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.reason: No 4625 or 4771 events at all in windows.security and no authentication-attempt tooling; the credential access in this window is LSASS dumping by hidden PowerShell on scranton, not brute force.

T1110.001.name: Password Guessing
T1110.001.reason: Zero failed logons (4625) across all hosts/users/logon types; all 297 4624 logons succeeded, mostly machine accounts.

T1110.002.name: Password Cracking
T1110.002.reason: No cracking tools, wordlists or potfiles were created or executed, but PowerShell.exe opened lsass.exe with 0x1fffff/0x1f3fff on scranton at 03:05:16 from a hidden monkey.png loader, consistent with dumping hashes for offline cracking.

T1110.003.name: Password Spraying
T1110.003.reason: No 4625/4771 failures; the 15 4648 explicit-credential logons are pbeesly PsExec runs to NASHUA plus DWM/UMFD/SCRANTON$ system artifacts, i.e. reuse of one known credential, not spraying.

T1110.004.name: Credential Stuffing
T1110.004.reason: No failed authentications and all 4624 source IPs are internal (10.0.x.x, 172.18.39.2, ::1, link-local); no stuffed credential lists observed.

T1111.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception
T1111.reason: No MFA/smartcard/NGC/PhoneFactor interception artifacts: a sysmon search for MultiFactor, MFA, Ngc, Wbio and PhoneFactor in win.TargetFilename, win.ImageLoaded and registry.path returned 0 hits. The LSASS handle hits are native Windows components (svchost.exe 289, wininit.exe/csrss.exe with 0x1fffff at 03:19:09 on scranton, wsmprovhost.exe PowerShell-remoting call trace on nashua) and SYSTEM-context PowerShell.exe; the only token-related script block is a Get-AttributesMask privilege enumeration from SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1 by pbeesly. SmartCardRoot registry reads are routine certificate-store enumeration. Malicious credential-access activity exists on scranton (C:\ProgramData\victim\*.scr reading the LSA key) but it is not MFA interception.

T1187.name: Forced Authentication
T1187.reason: No forced-authentication artifacts: all 66 SMB 139/445 connections came from process 'System' to internal addresses (10.0.0.4, 10.0.1.6, fe80::e40c:95b6:b0a7:6429); the only Startup .lnk (hostui.lnk) was written by PowerShell and targets a local binary, not a UNC/WebDAV path; no WebDAV/DavWWWRoot/@SSL paths, no 4104 blocks mentioning WebDAV/NTLM/Responder/PetitPotam, and no attacker SMB shares. The lone LsaSrv 6038 NTLM event on scranton is the standard once-per-boot informational warning. A separate malicious hostui.exe/registry-stager implant was found on scranton but it is persistence/execution, not T1187.

T1212.name: Exploitation for Credential Access
T1212.reason: 326 lsass process-access events are dominated by 0x1000/0x1400 masks from svchost.exe, AntimalwareConfig.exe and WindowsAzureTelemetryService.exe; the high-access outliers come from Windows components (wininit/csrss/services/svchost with lsm.dll, sysmain.dll, RPCRT4 call traces) and from PowerShell.exe/wsmprovhost.exe with managed .NET PowerShell call traces, not injected dumping code. No Mimikatz/sekurlsa/procdump/lsass strings in any 4104 script block or windows.other message. The credential theft actually present on scranton.dmevals.local (user pbeesly) is keystroke capture (Get-Keystrokes/View-Job 'Keystrokes') and plaintext credential reuse via PsExec64 -p, i.e. other techniques, not exploitation for credential access.

T1539.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
T1539.reason: No browser cookie/credential store was read, copied or exfiltrated on any host. C121/C122/C123/C124/C125 hits are false positives: Windows Search indexer (SearchProtocolHost.exe) launches, Edge's own _TempTestAccess.txt and a LocalService INetCookies container file, SYSTEM PowerShell module manifests mentioning 'chrome', and davclnt.dll DavSetCookie WebDAV auth cookies created by the exfil script. Zero 4663 accesses to Cookies/Login Data/Web Data and zero credential-dumping tool command lines; the PowerShell full-access handle on Edge processes at 03:05:17Z on scranton was not followed by any cookie-store access.

T1558.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
T1558.reason: No Kerberos ticket theft or forgery. Zeek Kerberos (2020-04-30 window) shows only normal AES256 AS/TGS for pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL against KDC 10.0.0.4; no RC4, no ticket anomalies. Rare LSASS handle masks come from SYSTEM components (wininit, csrss, svchost/lsm.dll, WindowsAzureTelemetryService) and from pbeesly PowerShell/wsmprovhost doing process enumeration. The scranton/nashua intrusion chain is credential-adjacent collection (private keys, keystrokes, clipboard, archives) but no ticket material was accessed.

T1558.001.name: Golden Ticket
T1558.001.reason: No golden-ticket indicators: no krbtgt hash extraction, no forged-TGT privilege anomalies. 4672 events are all NEWYORK$ machine-account logons with the standard machine privilege list; the only krbtgt TGS is a normal renewal by pbeesly; no krbtgt/golden/Mimikatz strings in any PowerShell script block.

T1558.002.name: Silver Ticket
T1558.002.reason: No silver-ticket indicators: all TGS requests are AES256 for cifs/NEWYORK, cifs/NASHUA, host/nashua.dmevals.local, ldap/NEWYORK.dmevals.local and HTTP/NASHUA by pbeesly, each preceded by a successful AS exchange; no silver/Mimikatz/service-ticket strings in script blocks; LSASS 0x1400/0x101001 accesses are .NET perf-counter and LSA policy reads.

T1558.003.name: Kerberoasting
T1558.003.reason: No Kerberoasting: only 11 TGS requests in the zeek window, all AES256 for a single principal, no RC4 etype-23 requests, no service-account TGS burst, and no kerberoast/Invoke-Kerberoast/GetUserSPNs/SPN strings in PowerShell script blocks.

T1558.004.name: AS-REP Roasting
T1558.004.reason: No AS-REP Roasting: every AS request returned KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED before succeeding with AES256, so pre-authentication was enforced; no asreproast/GetNPUsers/Rubeus command lines or script blocks.

T1606.reason: No forged web credentials. 4648 hits are PsExec (PSEXESVC.exe) and DWM/UMFD/machine-account logons; rare Sysmon 10 masks are svchost->wmiprvse, services/csrss->sppsvc, svchost->svchost with WMI/RPC call traces.

T1606.001.name: Web Cookies
T1606.001.reason: No cookie files written or forged (only a benign LocalService INetCookies path). The session does contain malicious activity (cod.3aka3.scr, PsExec with cleartext password, python.exe beaconing to 192.168.0.4:8443) but it is credential misuse/lateral movement, not web-cookie forging.

T1606.002.name: SAML Tokens
T1606.002.reason: All 4624 logons use standard Kerberos/Negotiate/NTLM packages and standard logon processes; no SAML/ADFS token artifacts or unusual authentication packages in the retrieved events.

T1649.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
T1649.reason: On scranton.dmevals.local, PowerShell (PID 3876, user pbeesly) read a persisted machine key and exported it (Security 5058 'Read persisted key from file' + 5059 'Export of persistent cryptographic key', RSA, key {ADA1F326-B4FE-4C0C-B68C-1B4CA6F364AC}, return 0x0) and in the same second wrote C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\coyn5igj.3io.pfx. The process was spawned by hidden, encoded PowerShell (IEX payload decoded from monkey.png) and the host also shows accesschk.exe writing 'passwordsDB', further hidden base64 PowerShell and a UAC-elevation attempt — certificate/private-key theft inside an active intrusion. checks.purpose: Detect PowerShell AS-REP roasting scripts.
Stack Kerberos request types to spot AS-REQ without preauthentication.
Stack successful logons by logon type to spot anomalous network/interactive logons that could indicate forged or replayed web credentials.
Stack explicit-credential logons (4648) by target account to find unusual accounts used with supplied credentials.
Stack process-access rights (Sysmon 10) to find rare access masks consistent with credential/token theft.
Stack file-creation targets (Sysmon 11) to find cookie/token files written by unusual processes.
Stack logon process names for successful logons to spot non-standard authentication packages that could indicate forged session material.
Stack authentication packages on successful logons to detect unusual packages that could accompany forged SAML/token-based logons.
Stack explicit-credential logons by account to find anomalous accounts used with supplied credentials.
Stack failed logons (4625) by target account to detect repeated authentication attempts consistent with MFA/credential abuse.
Stack failed logons by source IP to find a single source generating repeated authentication requests.
Stack registry value modifications (4657) to find changes to certificate-related registry keys.
Stack Kerberos TGT requests (4768) by account to spot anomalous certificate-based authentication.

findings.summary: On scranton.dmevals.local the pbeesly account ran a malicious PowerShell chain from 02:56Z to 03:08Z: a hidden, execution-policy-bypass PowerShell (PID 2976) launched from control.exe that decoded shellcode from a bitmap (monkey.png) and IEX'd it; registry Folder\shell\open\command hijack; archive of user documents (*pass*, *login*, *admin*, *.pst) into Draft.Zip; SysinternalsSuite deployment with sdelete64 anti-forensics; Invoke-Discovery, Invoke-Persistence, Get-PrivateKeys (exporting cert:\LocalMachine certs to .pfx with password 'saribas'), screen capture, Get-Keystrokes, Get-Clipboard, and Invoke-Exfil compressing Downloads to OfficeSupplies.7z with password 'lolol' and a WebDAV credential. This is credential-adjacent collection (private keys, keystrokes, clipboard) but no Kerberos ticket material was accessed: the only LSASS handle from this PowerShell (PID 2976, 0x1fffff at 03:05:16Z) has a call trace ending in an UNKNOWN module, and no ticket/kirbi/Rubeus/Mimikatz strings appear in any script block. Reported as suspicious for the intrusion, not as T1558 ticket theft.

findings.title: No web cookie theft/forging; instead malicious .scr execution and PsExec with plaintext password to run python.exe on NASHUA
findings.summary: No cookie files were written or forged: the only cookie-related file creation in the window is a benign INetCookies path under the LocalService WARP JIT package on scranton, and the only .json creations are WMI ConfigurationStatus files on newyork. However, the same host/user shows clearly malicious credential-access-adjacent activity that the cookie check surfaced indirectly. On scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T02:55:56Z user pbeesly launched C:\ProgramData\victim\â€®cod.3aka3.scr ("...scr" /S, parent explorer.exe, unsigned, no company/description), then at 03:02:04Z ran sdelete64.exe against that file from powershell.exe. From 03:11:18Z to 03:14:42Z pbeesly ran PsExec64.exe four times with the password supplied in cleartext on the command line (\\NASHUA -u dmevals\pbeesly -p <password> -i 2 C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe). On nashua.dmevals.local PSEXESVC.exe (installed by services.exe) spawned C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe as pbeesly, which then made repeated outbound TCP connections to 192.168.0.4:8443. This is credential misuse and lateral movement, not web-cookie forging, so T1606.001 itself is not observed; the activity is reported as suspicious because it is attacker tooling in the same session.

findings.title: No SAM hive dumping observed
findings.summary: No 4663/4656 access to SAM or SECURITY hive files, no reg save / SAM export command lines (the only 4688 command lines matching reg/save/sam were dsregcmd.exe and sc.exe start pushtoinstall registration), and no hive copy/rename of SAM in sysmon file-create-time events. The 4663 hits on ControlSet001\Control\Lsa are covered under T1003.004. No evidence of SAM database theft.

findings.title: No NTDS.dit theft observed
findings.summary: No sysmon file-create-time events referencing ntds, and no 4688 command lines containing ntds, vssadmin or ntdsutil. No NTDS extraction activity in the observed window.

findings.title: No cached domain credential (NL$/Cache) access observed
findings.summary: No 4663 or 4656 events referencing Cache or NL$ registry objects. Cached-credential harvesting was not observed; the credential access seen on scranton targeted LSASS memory and the Lsa key instead.

findings.title: Single 4662 DS-Replication-Get-Changes access by NEWYORK$ machine account — benign replication
findings.summary: Only one 4662 event in the whole dataset carries replication GUIDs: on newyork.dmevals.local at 2020-05-01T23:16:15Z, subject NEWYORK$ (S-1-5-18, logon 0x167eda) accessed object %{11487126-e2dc-4f51-acb1-1b0df0573bb5} with Properties {1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} (DS-Replication-Get-Changes) and {19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9}. The subject is the domain-joined machine account of the DC itself, not a user or attacker-controlled principal, and there is no accompanying drsuapi/lsadump/DCSync activity in sysmon, powershell or windows.other. Consistent with normal AD replication, not a DCSync attack.

findings.title: netsh trace capture on scranton.dmevals.local is Azure Network Watcher agent telemetry, not adversary sniffing
findings.summary: The only command-line hits for capture tooling were two netsh.exe invocations on scranton.dmevals.local (2020-05-01T23:19:17 and 23:19:24 local / 2020-05-02T03:19:17 and 03:19:24 UTC). The first runs 'netsh.exe trace start capture=yes traceFile="C:\windows\TEMP\E7116ECA-DFE6-43C7-8FA8-8D3AC5AA8726\B91E06C5-1C7C-4830-9A76-74FA211560A7.etl"' and the second 'netsh.exe trace stop'. In windows.security both events have process.parent.executable = C:\Packages\Plugins\Microsoft.Azure.NetworkWatcher.NetworkWatcherAgentWindows\1.4.1421.1\NetworkWatcherAgent\NetworkWatcherAgent.exe, i.e. the Azure Network Watcher VM extension performing a short (7 second) ETL packet capture into the agent's own TEMP GUID directory. In sysmon the same two netsh commands run as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and are immediately followed by Azure guest-agent logman.exe trace creation into C:\WindowsAzure\Logs (WaAppAgent.etl, RuntimeEvents.etl), confirming the Azure agent context. No pcap/npcap/wpcap driver image loads (C049 zero hits), no pktmon/dumpcap/windump/rawcap/Wireshark/tcpdump process creation anywhere in sysmon, and no PowerShell capture script blocks (C050 zero hits).

findings.title: javamtsup service on scranton.dmevals.local is a SysinternalsSuite artifact, not a packet-capture driver
findings.summary: The 7045 service-install stack contained one non-standard name, 'Java(TM) Virtual Machine Support Service' with ImagePath C:\Windows\System32\javamtsup.exe, installed on scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-01T23:04:15 local by account pbeesly (auto start, LocalSystem). The binary was not a capture driver: sysmon file-create events show it was extracted by powershell.exe from C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\SysinternalsSuite.zip into C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\SysinternalsSuite\javamtsup.exe at 2020-05-02T03:00:32, alongside 311 other SysinternalsSuite files (psping.exe, PsInfo64.exe, accesschk.exe, sdelete64.exe, PORTMON.HLP, etc.), and PowerShell 4104 records show pbeesly running Expand-Archive on SysinternalsSuite.zip, moving it to C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite, and invoking sdelete64.exe and accesschk.exe. When the service started (2020-05-02T03:19:14) it ran as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM from services.exe with no arguments and no network-capture behaviour. The remaining 7045 installs were PSEXESVC on nashua.dmevals.local (4x, demand start) and the standard per-user Windows services; no npcap/pcap/wpcap driver service was installed and no pcap image was ever loaded.

findings.title: No network sniffing observed in the Zeek window
findings.summary: The zeek dataset (2020-04-30T00:06:38Z..00:45:00Z, observers bobs.bigwheel.local and simplerockbuild.simplerock.lan) does not overlap any Windows dataset, so it was hunted on its own. Its 613 conn records are dominated by ssl (378), dns (39), krb_tcp (25), dce_rpc (20) and gssapi/smb combinations, with destination ports 8443 (376), 445 (45), 53 (37), 389 (30), 88 (25), 135 (14), 80 (12), 5985 (8) — a normal AD/file-share/web mix. The only anomalies are 12 'weird' records, 2 notices (SSL::Invalid_Server_Cert self-signed certificate to 192.168.0.5:443 and 192.168.0.4:8443) and a single conn from 10.0.1.4 to 192.168.0.5:1234. None of these show a host in promiscuous/ARP-spoofing or capture-tool posture, and sniffing is passive so it is not directly logged; no evidence of T1040 in this window.

findings.title: No keylogger artifacts found; screen/clipboard capture is the observed input-capture method
findings.summary: Searches for keylogging indicators returned nothing: no 4688 process creation with keylog/hook/GetAsyncKeyState command lines, no 4104 script blocks containing GetAsyncKeyState/keylog/SetWindowsHookEx, and no windows.other messages referencing keylog/GetAsyncKeyState/SetWindowsHookEx. The only service installs (7045) were PSEXESVC (4) and Java(TM) Virtual Machine Support Service (1), neither a keylogger. Registry writes (event 13/14) were dominated by W32Time, DeliveryOptimization, UserAssist and ContentDeliveryManager values with no keylogger persistence keys. Input capture on this host was performed via GUI screenshot/clipboard collection (reported under T1056.002), not a keystroke logger.

findings.title: No web portal capture observed
findings.summary: No IIS/web-shell activity was found: no file creations under \inetpub or .aspx/.asp files, no w3wp/appcmd/iisreset process creations, no 4663 object access to inetpub/aspx paths, and no PowerShell or windows.other records referencing inetpub/w3wp/IIS. Zeek HTTP traffic in its separate (non-overlapping) window consisted only of /webdav paths (OfficeSupplies.7z, python.exe) with no login/portal POSTs, so no credential-capturing web portal was identified.

findings.summary: Checks C087/C088/C089 returned no hits: there are no event.code 4625 events in windows.security for any host, user or logon type in the 2020-05-02 02:55-03:28 window. All 297 4624 logons are successful and dominated by machine accounts (NEWYORK$ 123, SYSTEM 60, SCRANTON$ 37, NASHUA$ 25) plus pbeesly (30), with no burst of failures against a single account. No guessing activity is observable.

findings.title: No password spraying: no 4625/4771 failures and no single password tried across many accounts
findings.summary: Checks C095/C096/C098 returned no hits (no 4625, no 4771). The 15 explicit-credential logons (4648) are 9 for pbeesly plus DWM-1/DWM-2/UMFD-0/UMFD-1/UMFD-2/SCRANTON$ system artifacts; the pbeesly 4648s are the PsExec64 -u dmevals\pbeesly -p ... runs from scranton to NASHUA (10.0.1.6) and the matching PSEXESVC.exe logons on nashua. That is reuse of one already-known credential against a single account, not spraying one password across many accounts.

findings.title: No credential stuffing: no failed logons and no external source IPs attempting authentication
findings.summary: Checks C099/C100/C101 returned no hits. All 297 successful 4624 logons originate from internal addresses only (::1, 10.0.1.4, 10.0.1.6, 10.0.0.4, 10.0.1.10, 10.0.1.5, 172.18.39.2, fe80:: link-local) with logon types 3/5/2/10/0; there is no list of distinct usernames tried against a service and no failed authentication to indicate stuffed credential lists.

findings.title: No MFA/smartcard interception tooling found; LSASS access on scranton/nashua is native Windows and PowerShell/.NET behaviour
findings.summary: Hunting for T1111 (Multi-Factor Authentication Interception) produced no evidence of MFA-provider, smartcard, NGC/Wbio or PhoneFactor artifacts: a search across windows.sysmon for win.TargetFilename/win.ImageLoaded/registry.path containing MultiFactor, MFA, Ngc, Wbio or PhoneFactor returned 0 hits, and no MFA/OTP interception tooling was observed. The LSASS process-access hits (326 events, win.TargetImage *lsass*) are dominated by C:\windows\system32\svchost.exe (289) plus Azure antimalware/telemetry agents (AntimalwareConfig.exe 15, WindowsAzureTelemetryService.exe 13). The rare high-access handles are native components: wininit.exe and csrss.exe with 0x1fffff and wininit.exe with 0x1000000 on scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:19:09.803Z (consistent with a boot/init sequence), svchost.exe with 0x101001 at 03:18:34.438Z and 0x3000 at 03:19:59.323Z, and wsmprovhost.exe with 0x1f3fff on nashua.dmevals.local at 03:09:29.430Z whose call trace runs through System.ni.dll and Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Management.ni.dll (a PowerShell remoting session, not credential theft). PowerShell.exe on scranton.dmevals.local opened lsass with 0x1f3fff at 03:05:16.623Z and 0x1fffff at 03:05:16.654Z, but the call trace is ntdll.dll/KERNELBASE.dll plus an UNKNOWN module and the account is NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (S-1-5-18); the only PowerShell script block on that host referencing tokens/privileges is a Get-AttributesMask helper (SE_GROUP_* constants) run by pbeesly from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1 at 2020-05-01T23:04:04, i.e. token/privilege enumeration, not MFA interception. The SmartCardRoot registry reads on scranton are generic certificate-store enumeration by powershell.exe and consent.exe. Note: the host does show other malicious activity (a .scr from C:\ProgramData\victim\ reading the LSA registry key as pbeesly), but that is credential-access/LSA reconnaissance, not MFA interception, so T1111 itself is not observed.

All 66 outbound SMB (139/445) connections in windows.sysmon were generated by process.executable 'System' (the kernel SMB client) on newyork, nashua, scranton and utica, and every destination was an internal address (10.0.0.4, 10.0.1.6, fe80::e40c:95b6:b0a7:6429) — normal domain-controller/file-server traffic, not attacker-controlled SMB/WebDAV listeners. The only shortcut written to a Startup folder (C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp\hostui.lnk) was created by PowerShell on scranton and targets a local binary, not a UNC/WebDAV path, so it is not a forced-auth .lnk. The single NTLM-related event (LsaSrv 6038 on scranton) is the standard once-per-boot informational warning that NTLM is in use, not evidence of coercion. No WebDAV/DavWWWRoot/@SSL paths, no 4104 script blocks referencing WebDAV/NTLM/Responder/PetitPotam, and no SMB share access to attacker shares were found.
findings.title: No forced-authentication (T1187) activity observed; SMB traffic is internal System-process client traffic

findings.summary: The T1212 hypothesis (exploitation for credential access) is not supported by the lsass access telemetry. Of 326 Sysmon event.code 10 accesses to C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe, 293 used GrantedAccess 0x1000 and 24 used 0x1400, and the high-access outliers are attributable to Windows components: svchost.exe (0x101001 via lsm.dll, 0x3000 via sysmain.dll), wininit.exe/csrss.exe (0x1fffff/0x1000000 at 03:19:09 during session-manager activity) and services.exe (0x1000 via RPCRT4). The two PowerShell.exe accesses on scranton.dmevals.local at 03:05:16 (0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff, CallTrace ending in UNKNOWN(000001996D28200D)) and the wsmprovhost.exe access on nashua.dmevals.local at 03:09:29 (0x1f3fff, CallTrace through System.ni.dll / Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Management.ni.dll) show managed PowerShell call stacks, i.e. .NET/PowerShell process enumeration rather than an injected memory-dumping payload; no Mimikatz/sekurlsa/procdump strings exist in any 4104 script block (C118 zero hits) and no lsass/mimikatz/procdump text in windows.other (C119 zero hits). The credential access that IS present on scranton.dmevals.local by user pbeesly is a different technique: a custom PowerShell toolkit (Keystroke-Check / Get-Keystrokes / View-Job 'Keystrokes' at 03:06:47-03:07:49, Invoke-BeachCleanup, Invoke-Exfil) plus plaintext credential use in PsExec64.exe -u dmevals\pbeesly -p <password> \\NASHUA at 03:11:18, followed by Kerberos/network logons as pbeesly to nashua.dmevals.local (8 type-3 Kerberos from 10.0.1.4, 8 type-2). Kerberos ticket activity (C116/C117) only shows pbeesly and machine accounts requesting normal SPNs (NEWYORK$, NASHUA$, SCRANTON$, krbtgt, WEC$). So T1212 exploitation for credential access is not observed; the intrusion itself is malicious but belongs to keystroke logging / credential reuse.
findings.title: No exploitation of lsass for credential access; credential theft on scranton was keystroke capture plus plaintext credential reuse

findings.title: No web session cookie theft observed; browser-store hits are Windows Search indexing and normal Edge activity
findings.summary: Across all four hosts (2020-05-02 02:55–03:28Z) no event shows a browser cookie/credential store being read, copied or exfiltrated. The C121 'Cookies/Login Data/Web Data' file-creation hits were false positives: the top values are lastalive0/1.dat and GroupPolicy DataStore files, plus one Edge _TempTestAccess.txt written by MicrosoftEdge.exe itself on scranton. The only INetCookies creation is a per-package container file written by svchost.exe (LocalService) on scranton at 03:21:05Z, i.e. normal Windows app-container behaviour. The C123 hits are four SearchProtocolHost.exe launches (parent SearchIndexer.exe) on scranton/nashua whose command line merely contains the Windows Search robot user-agent string — benign indexing. The C124 PowerShell hits on newyork are SYSTEM module manifests/localized-string blocks (xStorage, DNSClientCache, Nano-server test) that only mention 'chrome' incidentally; the scranton pbeesly blocks are the APT29-style toolkit (Invoke-ScreenCapture, Invoke-Exfil, Get-PrivateKeys, Invoke-BeachCleanup) which target screenshots, certificates and Downloads archives, not cookies. The only 'cookie' strings in process command lines are rundll32.exe davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie calls by pbeesly on scranton (03:08:50–03:10:23Z) — WebDAV auth cookies created for the \\192.168.0.4\webdav exfil drive, not stolen browser cookies. PowerShell did open MicrosoftEdge.exe/MicrosoftEdgeCP.exe/MicrosoftEdgeSH.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1fffff at 03:05:17Z on scranton, but no subsequent cookie-store file access (4663 on Cookies/Login Data/Web Data = 0 rows) or credential-dumping tooling (sharpweb/lazagne/mimikatz/sqlite command lines = 0 rows) followed. T1539 is therefore not observed; the credential-access activity present on scranton is certificate export (Get-PrivateKeys) and plaintext credentials in scripts, which fall outside this technique.

findings.title: Registry credential-key writes are Windows/IdentityCRL service noise, not harvesting
findings.summary: The 26 registry SetValue events touching Password/Credential/Winlogon/SAM paths are all routine OS activity: IdentityCRL ProviderPasswordLength/CharacterGroups, Winlogon PasswordExpiryNotification and VolatileUserMgrKey, CredentialEnrollmentManagerUserSvc_13619b service registration, DeviceGuard CredentialGuard\Enabled, and MuiCache entries. No reg query / reg save of HKLM\SAM or LSA Secrets was observed (the reg-query process check returned zero hits), and no process command line referenced SAM or NTDS. The single HKLM\SAM\SAM\Domains\Account\F write is a normal SAM hive value update, not a dump.

findings.summary: The only registry writes under Control\Lsa on scranton.dmevals.local were made by C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe itself at 03:19:09-03:19:10 (LsaPid = 0x2ec, LsaCfgFlagsDefault = 0, ProductType = 6), i.e. normal LSA startup state, not a Notification Packages / password filter registration. No file creation of a filter DLL in System32 or \Lsa\ was found, no 4657/4656 events referencing Notification Packages, and the only modules loaded into LSASS were the standard cryptdll.dll (32) and lsass.exe (1).

No adversary-in-the-middle positioning observed; credential theft on scranton/nashua used direct C2 and PsExec instead
findings.summary: Across windows.sysmon, windows.security, windows.other and zeek there is no evidence of an attacker interposing on network traffic. Sysmon event 22 DNS queries (81 total) contain only normal AD/DC discovery and Microsoft/telemetry lookups (NEWYORK.dmevals.local, _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.SCRANTON, wpad, v10.events.data.microsoft.com). Sysmon event 3 destinations are ordinary internal hosts plus public Microsoft/Azure addresses. The 4663/4656/4670 object-access stack is dominated by routine registry auditing (Session Manager\Environment, Lsa, Winlogon). The genuine malicious activity in this window is credential theft executed directly on hosts by user pbeesly (registry-stored payload run via Invoke-Expression on scranton, PsExec service installs on nashua, python.exe C2 to 192.168.0.4:8443), which is not AiTM.

findings.title: SMB traffic is normal Kerberos domain authentication; no LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning or SMB relay
findings.summary: Zeek conn records to port 445/139 show only 10.0.1.4 and 10.0.1.6 talking SMB to the domain controller 10.0.0.4 with krb/gssapi service identification, plus host-to-host SMB between 10.0.1.4 and 10.0.1.6 — consistent with normal domain logons, not relay. The only SMB attempts to 192.168.0.4 (445/139) were rejected (conn_state REJ) and were followed by HTTP to the same host, i.e. attacker C2 probing rather than a relay target. Sysmon 22 shows no LLMNR/NBT-NS style single-label lookups being answered by an unexpected host; the single-label queries (NASHUA, SCRANTON, NEWYORK, wpad) are ordinary and wpad.dmevals.local returned NXDOMAIN. Network logons (4624 type 3) are Kerberos from 10.0.1.4 for pbeesly and machine accounts, with no NTLM relay pattern. Service installs (4697/7045) are PsExec (PSEXESVC) and javamtsup by pbeesly, plus per-user svchost services — lateral movement, not relay.

findings.title: No ARP cache poisoning indicators; connection destinations are stable and expected
findings.summary: No ARP-level telemetry exists in these datasets, and the indirect indicators are clean: Sysmon event 3 destinations are consistent internal hosts (10.0.0.4, 10.0.1.4, 10.0.1.6, 192.168.0.4) and public Microsoft/Azure ranges, with no duplicated or shifting gateway MAC/IP pattern. DNS answers in zeek resolve internal names to their correct addresses (newyork.dmevals.local -> 10.0.0.4, nashua.dmevals.local -> 10.0.1.6, wec.dmevals.local -> 10.0.1.10). Network logons (4624 type 3) are Kerberos from 10.0.1.4, not replayed NTLM. The one anomalous TLS event is a self-signed certificate notice from 10.0.1.4 to 192.168.0.5:443, which is the attacker's own C2 endpoint contacted directly by the compromised host, not traffic redirected by ARP poisoning.

findings.title: No rogue DHCP server or DHCP option tampering; ipconfig/netsh activity is Azure Network Watcher
findings.summary: The only DHCP/network-configuration process activity is on scranton.dmevals.local at 03:19Z: netsh.exe 'trace start capture=yes' and 'trace stop' plus three 'ipconfig.exe /all' runs, all executed as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM with parent process NetworkWatcherAgent.exe (Microsoft Azure Network Watcher agent) — a benign diagnostic capture, not DHCP spoofing. Zeek has no traffic to UDP 67/68 (no DHCP server or client conversations), and windows.other contains no DHCP server events (1341/1342/1020/1063) and no PowerShell DHCP cmdlets. Logon process names for 4624 are Kerberos/Advapi/User32/NtLmSsp, with no unusual authentication source.

Across the 2020-05-02 window no evidence of Kerberos ticket theft or forgery was found. The only Kerberos protocol records are in the non-overlapping zeek window (2020-04-30 00:06-00:45Z): 35 kerberos events, all between 10.0.1.4/10.0.1.6 and the KDC 10.0.0.4, all for principal pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL, all using aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96, with normal AS (KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED then success) and TGS requests for cifs/NEWYORK, cifs/NASHUA, host/nashua.dmevals.local, ldap/NEWYORK.dmevals.local and HTTP/NASHUA. No RC4 (etype 23) ticket requests, no anomalous service-account TGS bursts, no krbtgt ticket anomalies. The rare LSASS handle accesses (0x1fffff, 0x1f3fff, 0x101001, 0x1000000, 0x3000) are all made by SYSTEM-context Windows components (wininit.exe, csrss.exe, svchost.exe/lsm.dll, WindowsAzureTelemetryService.exe/CorperfmonExt.dll) and by PowerShell/wsmprovhost running as pbeesly for process enumeration, not for credential dumping. The 4672 privileged-logon events are all NEWYORK$ machine-account logons with the standard machine privilege set.
findings.title: No Kerberos ticket theft/forgery observed; LSASS accesses are SYSTEM-context and unrelated to ticket abuse

findings.summary: No silver-ticket activity was observed. All TGS requests in the zeek window are AES256 (aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96) requests by pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL for cifs/NEWYORK, cifs/NASHUA, host/nashua.dmevals.local, ldap/NEWYORK.dmevals.local and HTTP/NASHUA, each preceded by a successful AS exchange with the KDC 10.0.0.4 - consistent with normal SMB/LDAP/HTTP authentication, not forged service tickets. No PowerShell script block referenced silver, Mimikatz or service ticket (check C258 zero hits). The LSASS accesses with service-account-relevant masks (0x1400 by WindowsAzureTelemetryService.exe via CorperfmonExt.dll, 0x101001 by svchost.exe via lsm.dll) are .NET performance-counter and LSA policy reads, not service-account hash theft.
findings.title: No silver-ticket indicators; service-ticket requests are ordinary AES256 TGS for pbeesly

findings.summary: No Kerberoasting was observed. The zeek Kerberos log shows only 11 TGS requests in the whole 2020-04-30 window, all AES256 and all for the single principal pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL, with no RC4 (etype 23) requests and no burst of service-ticket requests against service accounts. No PowerShell script block contained kerberoast, Invoke-Kerberoast, GetUserSPNs or SPN (check C264 zero hits). The 4624 logon stacking shows only machine accounts (NEWYORK$, SCRANTON$, NASHUA$, WEC$, UTICA$), SYSTEM, pbeesly and default DWM/UMFD accounts - no anomalous authentication with harvested Kerberos material.
findings.title: No Kerberoasting: no RC4 TGS bursts or SPN enumeration tooling

findings.summary: No AS-REP Roasting was observed. Every AS request in the zeek window (14 AS records from 10.0.1.4 and 10.0.1.6 to the KDC 10.0.0.4) first returned KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED and was then completed successfully with AES256 - i.e. pre-authentication was enforced for pbeesly, so no account was roastable. No process creation with asreproast, GetNPUsers or Rubeus command lines (check C267 zero hits) and no PowerShell script block containing asreproast, GetNPUsers, Rubeus or preauth (check C269 zero hits).
findings.title: No AS-REP Roasting: all AS exchanges required pre-authentication
No forged web credentials observed; hits explained by PsExec lateral movement and system process-access noise
findings.summary: The T1606 check hits do not show forged web credentials. The 4648 explicit-credential logons (15 total) are dominated by pbeesly authenticating to NASHUA via PsExec (win.ProcessName C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe, TargetServerName localhost, SubjectUserName NASHUA$) plus routine DWM-/UMFD-/machine-account logons from winlogon.exe/wininit.exe/taskhostw.exe. The rare Sysmon 10 access masks (0x101541, 0x101441, 0x103800/0x103801, 0x1014c0) are all system-to-system accesses: svchost.exe->wmiprvse.exe (WMI), services.exe->sppsvc.exe, csrss.exe->sppsvc.exe, svchost.exe->svchost.exe (appinfo/RPC), with call traces in wmiprvsd.dll, basesrv.dll, appinfo.dll and RPCRT4.dll. The 0x1fffff full-access grants are likewise csrss.exe/svchost.exe/services.exe/conhost.exe/PSEXESVC.exe opening normal child processes. No forged credential material was found. Note: the surrounding activity IS malicious (see T1606.001 finding) but it is credential theft/lateral movement, not web-credential forging.

findings.title: No SAML token forging; logon packages are standard Kerberos/Negotiate
findings.summary: All 297 successful 4624 logons use standard authentication packages (Kerberos 217, Negotiate 78, NTLM 1, '-' 1) and standard logon processes (Kerberos 217, Advapi 76, User32 2, NtLmSsp 1, '-' 1); there is no SAML/ADFS/token-signing component, no unusual authentication package, and no token or federation artifact in the file-creation data. The 4648 explicit-credential events are the same PsExec/DWM/UMFD/machine-account set described above. Nothing in the retrieved events indicates forged SAML tokens.

findings.title: Sysmon self-signed certificate written to ROOT store on nashua.dmevals.local (benign)
findings.summary: The only SystemCertificates registry modification in the window is on nashua.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:16:19Z: Security 4657 shows the value 'Blob' of \REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SystemCertificates\ROOT\Certificates\BE36A4562FB2EE05DBB3D32323ADF445084ED656 modified by process C:\Windows\Sysmon.exe running as NASHUA$ (S-1-5-18, logon 0x3E7), with matching 4663 read/write access on the same key by Sysmon.exe. Sysmon creates and installs its own self-signed certificate for config/archive signing, and the corresponding certificate file C:\Windows\System32\config\systemprofile\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\SystemCertificates\My\Certificates\A4F69156AB2E4C5AFBB55BFD66DC60F0D398FE9A was created by C:\windows\Sysmon.exe at the same timestamp. No attacker tooling, no key export and no non-Sysmon process touched the certificate stores on this host.

findings.title: Kerberos TGT requests show no certificate-based (PKINIT) authentication
findings.summary: All 14 Kerberos 4768 TGT requests in the window were logged on newyork.dmevals.local for pbeesly (9) and the machine account SCRANTON$ (5), all with PreAuthType 2 (encrypted timestamp, i.e. password-based pre-authentication, not PKINIT/certificate pre-auth), TicketEncryptionType 0x12 (AES-256) and Status 0x0. No certificate-based logon or forged-ticket indicator is present in the Kerberos data; the TGT volume is consistent with normal workstation logon/renewal behaviour.

incidents.title: Credential-access toolchain staged and executed from user-writable paths (SysinternalsSuite, psversion.ps1, accesschk, sdelete, PsExec)

incidents.title: LSASS memory access with full-access masks by attacker PowerShell on scranton and wsmprovhost on nashua
incidents.rationale: All describe the same LSASS handle-open events: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976) on scranton opening lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff and UNKNOWN call trace, and wsmprovhost.exe on nashua with 0x1f3fff. This is LSASS memory access, best fit T1003.001.

incidents.title: LSA registry key read by pbeesly's processes on scranton
incidents.rationale: 4663/4673 events on HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Lsa consistent with LSA secrets access; best fit T1003.004.

incidents.title: PowerShell screen capture and clipboard harvesting on scranton
incidents.rationale: Invoke-ScreenCapture and Get-Clipboard in pbeesly's PowerShell session; GUI input capture, best fit T1056.002.

incidents.title: No brute-force authentication attempts observed
incidents.rationale: Finding explicitly assesses brute force as not observed; the only credential-access signal is LSASS access. Retained under T1110 as the technique it evaluated.

incidents.title: No password-cracking tooling or hash files found
incidents.rationale: Finding evaluates password cracking and finds no cracking artifacts; only LSASS handle access stands out. Retained under T1110.002 as the technique it evaluated.

incidents.title: Hardcoded plaintext credentials in attacker tooling on scranton
incidents.rationale: Same embedded plaintext credentials (saribas, cozy/MyCozyPassw0rd!, Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by) in tooling; unsecured credentials, best fit T1552.

incidents.title: Credential-bearing files staged and archived on scranton and nashua
incidents.rationale: Same passwordsDB, Draft.Zip, OfficeSupplies.7z and working.zip collection/archiving events; credentials in files, best fit T1552.001.

incidents.title: Private key and certificate export to password-protected .pfx on scranton
incidents.rationale: Same Get-PrivateKeys action exporting LocalMachine certificates/private keys to a .pfx in Downloads; best fit T1552.004.

incidents.title: PowerShell opens LSASS with full access on scranton and nashua (credential store access)
incidents.rationale: F65 (hostui.exe reading Explorer memory) and F66/F67 (malicious .scr execution and sdclt UAC-bypass burst) are grouped here as the surrounding credential-store/UI-harvesting activity; best fit T1555 for the credential-store access context.

incidents.title: Credential theft and lateral movement by pbeesly; no authentication-process modification
incidents.rationale: Finding evaluates authentication-process modification and finds none; the observed action is credential theft plus lateral movement. Retained under T1556 as the technique it evaluated.

incidents.title: No hybrid-identity backdoor; service installs are PsExec/Java
incidents.rationale: Finding evaluates hybrid identity modification and finds only PSEXESVC and Java service installs. Retained under T1556.007 as the technique it evaluated.

incidents.title: No web cookie theft/forging; malicious .scr execution and PsExec with plaintext password
incidents.rationale: Finding evaluates web cookie forging and finds none; observed activity is execution and lateral movement. Retained under T1606.001 as the technique it evaluated.

incidents.title: Persistent RSA machine key exported and written to .pfx on scranton
incidents.rationale: Security 5058/5059 key read and export by pbeesly's PowerShell producing a .pfx; steal or forge authentication certificates, best fit T1649.

incidents.title: hostui.exe persistence and registry-stored base64 PowerShell stager on scranton
incidents.rationale: Startup .lnk and HKLM registry base64 stager with hostui.bat execution is persistence/execution, not credential access.
